CPU-Z and GPU-Z readings showed sustained power consumption above 610 W during DLSS 5 testing, while the 16-pin connector is theoretically rated to handle up to 600 W plus an additional 75 W from the PCIe slot. The connector became so damaged that disconnecting the power cable was difficult due to melted plastic bonding the connector to the card's socket. Reported impact The MSI GeForce RTX 5090 Gaming Trio OC became non-functional after the connector failure. Multiple pins on the 16-pin power connector showed significant damage from overheating. Index analysis DLSS 5 uses AI-assisted rendering that substantially increases computational load on the GPU compared to standard rasterization. The technology's power demands exposed a weakness in the connection between the power supply and the graphics card, either due to insufficient connector specifications or improper seating of the connector.
AII-1000-50983: President Donald Trump shared an AI-generated image on Truth Social depicting actor Robert De Niro holding a shirt reading 'TRUMP IS MY PRESIDENT,' with the caption 'Even this jerk is beginning to get it!' The image was one of dozens shared by Trump on Truth Social on Sunday. Independent analysts and AI-detection tools verified the image as AI-generated. The Hive Moderation tool rated it as 99.5 percent likely to be AI-generated, specifically identifying OpenAI's GPT-4o model. The OpenAI Verify tool detected an embedded SynthID watermark confirming it was synthesized using OpenAI's digital generation tools. Reported impact De Niro, a long-standing and vocal critic of Trump for over a decade, has not issued a statement about the specific image. The falsification misrepresents De Niro's publicly documented opposition to Trump, whom he has called 'evil,' a 'tyrant,' and said will 'destroy' America. Index analysis The incident demonstrates use of deepfake imagery to misrepresent a public figure's political position. The image was deliberately crafted to suggest that a known Trump critic had reversed his stance, contradicting years of documented public statements.
AII-1000-54483: Approximately 5,000 gallons of diesel fuel spilled from a storage tank at an Equinix data center in Secaucus, New Jersey on Friday night. According to the mayor of Secaucus, the spill was caused by a computer glitch. Equinix detected the fuel release, stopped it, and immediately contacted agencies. Contractors removed the spilled oil from nearby Anderson Creek, a tributary of the Hackensack River, with approximately 3,500 gallons cleaned up over the weekend. Reported impact The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection stated that the spill was contained before reaching the Hackensack River itself. The agency and U.S. Coast Guard monitoring found no observed impacts to the river or wildlife. The DEP noted there are no drinking water intakes in the area and no impacts to wildlife have been reported. Cleanup was expected to take several days. Index analysis The spill highlighted concerns about data center expansion and reliance on diesel backup generators for power. Data centers have become a political issue due to concerns about environmental and economic effects of artificial intelligence infrastructure. Governance controls Equinix stated it was conducting a full investigation to determine the root cause and prevent recurrence, and brought in an environmental remediation company. The company said it has been in the community for over two decades and committed to resolving the issue transparently.
AII-1000-51951: US content creator Kalie Robbins uploaded a video to Facebook of herself singing with her daughter in a car. Meta AI displayed a suggested question, 'Who's the child passenger?', below the post. When Robbins clicked the prompt, Meta AI reportedly surfaced information about her children including their names, birth details, photographs and videos. Robbins claimed some material came from posts shared by other family members years earlier, including a newborn photograph posted by her mother. Robbins said Meta AI also suggested the question 'Where does Kalie Robbins live?' and appeared to connect information from older posts about her previous residences with recent location details, despite the original video containing no location information. Robbins claimed she had deleted one photograph from her own Facebook account long ago, yet it appeared in the AI results. Reported impact Robbins expressed concern that years of fragmented family photographs and posts could be assembled by AI into a detailed digital profile of her minor children without her full understanding of how the information would be connected. She said she had not realised that seemingly unrelated posts could be combined to create a comprehensive picture of her children's lives. Following the experience, Robbins said she planned to remove identifiable photographs and videos of her children from her social media accounts and urged friends and relatives to do the same. Index analysis The incident highlights how AI systems can aggregate and cross-reference information from multiple fragmented social media posts, including content shared by other family members and material users believed they had deleted, to create profiles of individuals, particularly minors.
AII-1000-51157: Criminals are using facial comparison technology to locate people with physical characteristics similar to their own, then attempting to impersonate those individuals during identity validation processes. The strategy, termed 'golpe do sósia' (lookalike scam), exploits facial recognition systems by having fraudsters pass themselves off as other people during account openings and registrations. According to Serasa Experian's analytical intelligence team, criminals use tools capable of comparing their own face against images in various databases, including illegally obtained ones, to identify legitimate identities with high physical similarity. The fraudster then selects an identity deemed most likely to pass biometric validation and attempts to use that person's data in fraud schemes. Reported impact Serasa Experian's anti-fraud solutions identified and blocked 2.86 million identity fraud attempts in the first half of 2026, a 32.9% increase compared to the same period in 2025. The blocked attempts were associated with an estimated R$ 3.77 billion in prevented losses during the period. Index analysis The new tactic reverses traditional identity fraud logic: criminals begin with their own face, search for physically similar people, identify potential victims, then attempt to use that victim's identity data in fraud. According to Leandro Bartolassi, director of Authentication and Fraud Prevention at Serasa Experian, the strategy demonstrates how criminals can exploit technologies designed to increase security. Governance controls Serasa Experian recommends that facial recognition not be used as the sole authentication layer. The company advocates combining facial recognition with other signals including document validation, liveness checks, data verification, device analysis, behavioral pattern identification, and additional risk signal evaluation to detect inconsistencies that facial analysis alone would miss.
